title: Investment Appraisal
description: Evaluate capital expenditure decisions using NPV, IRR, and payback period. Tests financial technique application and sensitivity analysis.

seo.overviewTitle: Investment Appraisal & Capital Budgeting (NPV / IRR / Payback)
seo.overviewBody: Capital budgeting evaluates major corporate investment projects to ensure long-term value creation. Financial managers prove decision-making rigor by evaluating Net Present Value (NPV), Internal Rate of Return (IRR), Payback Period, and Profitability Index.

deliverables.title: 1. Capital Investment Evaluation Model
deliverables.desc: Capital budgeting spreadsheet (.xlsx) modeling initial outlays, operating cash flows, NPV, IRR, and payback period.

deliverables.title: 2. NPV & IRR Scenario Comparison Memo
deliverables.desc: Executive memo comparing competing capital project proposals under different hurdle discount rates.

deliverables.title: 3. Risk & Payback Period Sensitivity Analysis
deliverables.desc: Sensitivity analysis evaluating project breakeven timelines under pessimistic cash flow assumptions.

faqs.question: Why is NPV theoretically superior to the Payback Period method?
faqs.answer: NPV accounts for the time value of money and evaluates all cash flows across the entire project lifecycle, whereas Payback Period ignores cash flows after breakeven.

faqs.question: What does Internal Rate of Return (IRR) represent?
faqs.answer: IRR is the exact discount rate at which the Net Present Value (NPV) of a project's cash flows equals zero.

faqs.question: What should you do when NPV and IRR give conflicting project rankings?
faqs.answer: Always rely on Net Present Value (NPV) because it measures absolute currency value added to shareholder wealth.
